chunks: From him, from Fudayl ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, who said:
"When you enter the mosque, say: 'O Allah, forgive my sins and open for me the doors of Your mercy. And when you leave, say: 'O Allah, forgive me and open for me the doors of Your bounty.'"
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications for entering and leaving the mosque in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith outlines the spiritual etiquette of transitioning between the mundane world and the sacred space of the mosque, emphasizing the mosque as a conduit for divine grace. The distinction between 'doors of mercy' (rahmah) upon entry and 'doors of bounty' (fadl) upon exit reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of the mosque as a place where one receives initial spiritual sustenance and departs with accumulated blessings for worldly and otherworldly success.
